channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Researchers took over cold-chain refrigeration controllers and hid the temperature rise while food spoiled
item.description: Claroty’s Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory refrigeration controllers, 21 of them high severity, which chain together — authentication flaws, predictable administrator credentials and command injection — to bypass security controls and reach root-level remote code execution. A separate disclosure covers three flaws in Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers, including a hidden ‘code-of-the-day’ authentication mechanism that sidesteps normal login and leads to code execution. What makes this a food story rather than an HVAC one is the demonstration: researchers showed a compromised controller remotely manipulating cooling fans and compressors while concealing the resulting temperature rise from operators, so product degrades without an alarm ever sounding. Copeland has released firmware 1.13 and Danfoss R4.3.1. These controllers sit in cold storage, processing plants, distribution centres and retail back-of-house. - Claroty Team82 research; SecurityWeek — vendor-confirmed, fixes released - Published week of 10–14 Aug 2026; Copeland and Danfoss fixes available

item.title: [High] Coca-Cola suspended US fairlife production after ransomware reached production-related systems
item.description: Coca-Cola disclosed on 16 July that its fairlife dairy subsidiary identified unauthorized third-party access to a portion of its systems, including production-related systems, in connection with a ransomware event, and that production operations at fairlife in the United States were temporarily suspended. Reporting centred on the ERP layer carrying scheduling, material movement and order execution. It is the cleanest recent illustration of a food manufacturer losing output without an attacker addressing a controller — at an operator with resources far beyond a typical processor. The disclosure also landed within days of Japanese food and cold-chain logistics company Nichirei confirming a cyberattack that caused system failures across its group from 13 July, underlining that the exposure is not US-specific. - Coca-Cola disclosure; Cybersecurity Dive, TechCrunch, Industrial Cyber - Disclosed 16 Jul 2026 — US production temporarily suspended

item.title: [High] Six agencies warn on Gunra ransomware — VPN gateways and firewalls are the documented way in
item.description: Joint advisory AA26-222A, published 10 August by CISA, the FBI, DC3, NSA, the Secret Service and South Korea’s National Police Agency, covers Gunra ransomware. Gunra appeared in April 2025 built on leaked Conti source code and has grown into a ransomware-as-a-service operation recruiting affiliates through dark-web forums. Affiliates break in through exposed edge infrastructure — VPN gateways, firewall appliances and RDP-reachable systems — then exfiltrate before encrypting under double extortion. Named victim sectors include manufacturing, transport, utilities, retail and government. Food and beverage operators should read the entry-point list literally: the appliance a filler-line OEM or a refrigeration contractor dials through for support is the same class of device the advisory describes. - CISA/FBI/NSA joint advisory AA26-222A - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos: 70 food and beverage ransomware incidents in Q2, none involving direct control-system manipulation
item.description: Dragos’ Q2 2026 industrial ransomware analysis, published 11 August, recorded 1,140 incidents at industrial organizations, up 12% from 1,020 in Q1. Food and beverage organizations accounted for 70; manufacturing overall took 747, transportation and logistics 95, and ICS-adjacent firms such as engineering companies and system integrators 117. North America led with 514 incidents, Europe 316. Dragos observed no case in the quarter where a ransomware operator directly manipulated an industrial control system, while noting that disrupting the IT systems supporting industrial environments is enough to interrupt production. For food and agriculture the 117 integrator and engineering-firm victims deserve attention too: those firms hold recipe libraries, line drawings and standing remote access to your plants. - Dragos Industrial Ransomware Analysis Q2 2026; Help Net Security - Published 11 Aug 2026 (covering Q2 2026)

item.title: [High] AA26-097A update: engineering software used to strip shutdown and alarm logic from PLCs
item.description: The 22 July update to joint advisory AA26-097A describes Iran-affiliated actors connecting to internet-exposed controllers using the vendors’ own engineering software — Rockwell Studio 5000 Logix Designer, Schneider EcoStruxure Control Expert and Siemens TIA Portal — over ports 44818, 2222, 102, 502 and 22, then extracting, modifying and deleting project logic. In one US case investigators found a project file that preserved ladder logic for downstream function while adding logic that overrode safe operating parameters and disabled shutdown and alarm functions, letting equipment enter unsafe states without notifying operators. Targeted families include Rockwell CompactLogix and Micro850, Schneider Modicon M340 (BMX P34) and Siemens S7-1200. In a processing plant those controllers run pasteurisers, CIP skids, fillers and cooking or chilling steps where the alarm and interlock logic is the food-safety control. - CISA/FBI/NSA/EPA joint advisory AA26-097A; SecurityWeek - Updated 22 Jul 2026 (originally published 7 Apr 2026) — campaign ongoing

item.title: [Critical] CVSS 10 unauthenticated root command injection in Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway (ICSA-26-225-02)
item.description: CISA released 14 ICS advisories on 13 August, led by CVE-2026-19188 in the Haiwell IoT Cloud HMI Gateway at CVSS 10.0. The device’s ‘Net Check’ feature passes user-supplied input from the cmdPing Socket.io event to the operating system without sanitizing it, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary OS commands as root without user interaction. Version 3.40.1.12 is affected; CISA lists critical manufacturing, energy and water among the deployment sectors. Food operators meet this class of device on OEM packaging skids, remote grain and silo monitoring, irrigation and pivot control, and cold-store telemetry — equipment bought as a machine rather than as an IT asset, often with a SIM card supplied by the vendor and no one on site who knows it is reachable. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-225-02 - Published 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] August ICS Patch Tuesday: maximum-severity authentication bypass in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050
item.description: Siemens published 10 advisories on 11 August, headed by a maximum-severity missing-authentication flaw in SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices (SSA-834709) that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with elevated privileges. Siemens also fixed a critical code-execution flaw in Siveillance Video Management Servers and high-severity issues in Solid Edge, Simcenter Nastran, the Siemens License Server, Simcenter Femap, Parasolid and Logo! Soft Comfort, with medium-severity fixes in Ruggedcom devices and Desigo controllers. Schneider Electric covered NetBotz 5 and PowerChute Serial Shutdown; Phoenix Contact addressed multiple PLCnext firmware flaws exploitable without authentication; Honeywell issued several building-management advisories. In a food plant the entries that bite are usually the quiet ones — NetBotz environmental monitoring in a server room, PowerChute on a UPS-backed SCADA host, Desigo running plant HVAC. - Siemens ProductCERT, Schneider Electric, Phoenix Contact and Honeywell PSIRT via SecurityWeek - Advisories published 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco Secure Firewall ASA/FTD zero-day added to CISA KEV after denial-of-service exploitation
item.description: CISA added three vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August, including CVE-2026-20349, a heap-inspection flaw in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Firewall Threat Defense that Cisco patched after exploitation as a zero-day for denial-of-service attacks. The others are a use-after-free in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (CVE-2026-68820) and SQL injection in Metabase (CVE-2026-72898). Earlier in August CISA added Progress LoadMaster CVE-2026-8037 and flaws in Langflow, Apache Tomcat and N-able N-central. The Gunra advisory names this exact class of appliance as an entry point, which is why a firewall patch belongs on the plant availability agenda: multi-site processors often route every DC and cold store through one pair of these boxes. - CISA KEV catalog additions, 5, 7 and 11 Aug 2026 - Cisco ASA/FTD added to KEV 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [Low] Senate farm bill markup ends without advancing, leaving sector cyber provisions in committee
item.description: The Senate Agriculture Committee held a markup of the Agricultural Act of 2026 — the Senate’s version of the 2026 Farm Bill — on 6 August. The motion to report the legislation to the full Senate failed 10–11, so the bill did not advance out of committee. Cybersecurity provisions attached to farm bill vehicles include support for precision-agriculture adoption through public-private partnerships on cybersecurity and interoperability in the House version. Separately, the Farm and Food Cybersecurity Act (S.754 / H.R.1604) would direct USDA, working with CISA, to conduct a biennial risk assessment of cyber threats to the food and agriculture sector and run annual crisis simulation exercises, authorizing $1 million a year from 2026 through 2030. Neither changes anything an operator must do today. - National Association of Counties markup report; Congress.gov (S.754 / H.R.1604) - Senate Agriculture Committee markup 6 Aug 2026 — motion to report failed 10–11
